plugins.name: AdGuard Home
plugins.description: Registers your devices in AdGuard Home as DNS rewrites (Filters, DNS rewrites): an A record for every device Netlens knows and DNS does not, and a changed address for devices whose IP changed (DHCP). Netlens only changes rewrites it wrote itself (it remembers them, AdGuard Home has no comment field) and never touches rewrites you or anything else made.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: AdGuard Home v0.107 (tested in a lab and verified on a real installation)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: ASUS router (AiMesh)
plugins.description: Built into Netlens: which device is connected to which AiMesh node, with Wi-Fi signal and roaming (stock ASUSWRT, read-only, no SSH).
plugins.author: Netlens

plugins.name: BIND 9
plugins.description: Registers your devices in a BIND 9 (or any RFC 2136 compatible) DNS server: an A record and a reverse (PTR) record for every device Netlens knows and DNS does not, and a changed address for devices whose IP changed (DHCP). Reads zones by zone transfer (AXFR) and writes by dynamic update (RFC 2136), both signed with a TSIG key. Every change is guarded by a prerequisite, so a record that changed meanwhile is never overwritten. Netlens only changes records it remembers writing.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Other RFC 2136 servers with TSIG (not tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Caddy
plugins.description: Shows the sites a Caddy 2 web server publishes as a reverse proxy: domains, the upstream address and port, redirects, and whether Caddy makes the HTTPS certificate itself. Netlens ties every site to the device or container behind it, keeps an HTTPS check per site and can give the domains a DNS name. Read-only: it only reads Caddy's admin API (GET /config/). Caddy's admin API has no password: it must only be reachable from a network you trust.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Docker hosts
plugins.description: Shows your Docker hosts with their containers: state, health, restarts, image (and how old it is), compose project, published ports, and containers with their own address on your network (macvlan / ipvlan) matched to the devices Netlens found. Optionally flags containers that have a newer image in their registry. Read-only, through a read-only socket proxy (the README has the recipe). Tested on Docker 29.8.2 with a bridge-network setup; macvlan and ipvlan are tested with simulated data only.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Containers on macvlan / ipvlan networks (not yet tested on a real host)

releases.changelog: Adds a dashboard card with running, stopped, restarting and paused containers (Customize on the dashboard). Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

New setting Check for newer images (off by default): Netlens asks the registry each image comes from whether its tag now points to a newer image and flags those containers, with an event. Only image names are sent. Needs IMAGES: 1 on the socket proxy and Netlens 0.3.119 or newer.
The settings page has a collapsed box with the docker-compose lines for the read-only socket proxy that every Docker host needs, with a Copy button. Needs Netlens 0.3.115 or newer.

tested_on: Docker Engine 29.8.2 through tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy, three real hosts (bridge networks)
review.notes: Read-only: only GET requests through the socket proxy. Tested on three real Docker hosts. Macvlan and ipvlan matching is tested with simulated data only.

releases.changelog: Hosts are entered as a list: one line per Docker host (proxy address, and the host's own address under More), a Test button per line, and Test all. Existing settings carry over. Needs Netlens 0.3.109 or newer.

First release. Docker hosts and their containers as guests of the host: state, health, restarts, image and its age, compose project, published ports, and macvlan / ipvlan containers matched to devices. Needs Netlens 0.2.106 or newer.

plugins.name: Example router
plugins.description: A template plugin that reports a made-up router, access point and two clients. Install it to see how plugins work, then copy it as a starting point for your own.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release.

review.notes: Maintainer-written template: the code is about 40 lines, contacts nothing and returns made-up data.

plugins.name: HAProxy
plugins.description: Shows the backends of an HAProxy load balancer as sites: the first healthy server of each backend as the upstream (address and port), and whether the backend is in maintenance. HAProxy's statistics do not contain host names, so you can list them per backend yourself, otherwise the sites show without a domain. Netlens ties every backend to the device or container behind it. Read-only: it only reads the statistics page (CSV).
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Microsoft Hyper-V
plugins.description: Shows your Hyper-V hosts with their virtual machines (state, processors, memory, start time, network switch) and ties each VM to the device Netlens found by MAC address, then IP. Reads through Windows Remote Management over HTTPS by running one fixed, read-only Get-VM script; the settings page has the PowerShell lines that create the user and the HTTPS listener. Tested on a real Windows 11 Hyper-V host (user without administrator rights) and with simulated answers.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Hyper-V on Windows Server and Windows 10/11 Pro through WinRM over HTTPS (tested on Windows 11 24H2)
NTLM or Basic login; Kerberos is not supported

releases.changelog: Adds a dashboard card with running, stopped and paused virtual machines. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

Reads the virtual machines through Hyper-V's management data (CIM) instead of Get-VM, which Windows refuses for a user without administrator rights. The setup lines also let 'Remote Management Users' open a remote shell (WinRM permission). Tested on a real Windows 11 host.
Setup lines give the groups by id (Remote Management Users, Hyper-V Administrators), so they work on Windows in any language, and print the members to check. A clearer message for 'access is denied'.
First release. Virtual machines of a Hyper-V host through WinRM over HTTPS, matched to devices by MAC address then IP. Needs Netlens 0.3.115 or newer.

plugins.name: Incus / LXD
plugins.description: Shows an Incus (or LXD) server or cluster: the servers as hosts and every container and virtual machine as a guest, with state, MAC and IP addresses (when the instance sits on your LAN rather than behind NAT), image, CPU and memory limits, and autostart. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with a client certificate that you add to the trust store as restricted.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Incus virtual machines and clusters, LXD (not tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Kong Gateway
plugins.description: Shows the routes a Kong Gateway (OSS or Enterprise, DB-less or with a database) publishes: host names, the upstream service address and port, protocols (http, https, tcp) and whether a route is enabled. Netlens ties every route to the device or container behind it, can keep an HTTPS check per site and can register the host names in DNS. Read-only: it only sends GET requests to the Admin API.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Kong with a database and Kong Enterprise (not tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Kubernetes
plugins.description: Shows a Kubernetes cluster (k3s, kubeadm, RKE2, Talos, microk8s, ...) as hosts and guests: the nodes as hosts with their address and Ready state, the pods as guests of the node they run on, with namespace, workload, image, ports, restarts and readiness. Read-only: it only lists nodes and pods with a service account that may do nothing else. Pods that finished (Completed jobs) are left out.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: MikroTik RouterOS
plugins.description: Reads a MikroTik router, switch or access point (RouterOS 7.1+): the device as a network node, MikroTik neighbours (MNDP/LLDP) as child nodes, and the devices it knows as clients with their bridge port, DHCP lease, ARP entry or Wi-Fi registration (band, signal, link speed). Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy and to show Wi-Fi signal history. Read-only: only GET requests to the REST API.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Wi-Fi registration tables and MNDP neighbours (not tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: NetBox
plugins.description: Imports your documented network from NetBox (4.x): devices with a network role (router, switch, access point ...) become network nodes, every other device a client, and the cables between interfaces decide who hangs below whom, including the port a device is plugged into. Netlens matches them to what it finds on the network by MAC address, so the hierarchy shows your documentation. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with an API token that has read-only permissions.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: HashiCorp Nomad
plugins.description: Shows a Nomad cluster as hosts and guests: the client nodes as hosts with their address, state and eligibility, and the allocations (running tasks of your jobs) as guests of the node they run on, with namespace, job, image, published ports, restarts and start time. Read-only: it only reads nodes and allocations, with an ACL token that has the read-job and node read capabilities if your cluster uses ACLs.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Nginx Proxy Manager
plugins.description: Shows the sites your Nginx Proxy Manager publishes (proxy hosts, redirections, streams, 404 hosts) and ties each to the device or Docker container behind it: a card on that device, the sites a proxy serves, certificate expiry events, optional HTTPS checks per site and optional DNS names for the domains. Read-only, through a user that can only view. Tested on Nginx Proxy Manager 2.15.1 (login and permission checks on a real instance; site data with simulated answers).
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Nginx Proxy Manager 2.15.x (login tested on a real instance)
Sites, certificates and access lists read with simulated data matching the 2.x API

releases.changelog: Adds a dashboard card with the number of sites, switched-off sites, proxy hosts, redirections, streams and 404 hosts. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

First release. Proxy hosts, redirections, streams and 404 hosts with their certificates, tied to the device or container behind each site; certificate expiry events; optional HTTPS check per site; optional DNS names. Needs Netlens 0.3.116 or newer.

plugins.name: TP-Link Omada
plugins.description: Reads an Omada controller (5.1 or newer): gateway, switches and access points, which device hangs below which, and which switch or access point each client is connected to, with Wi-Fi signal, band and link rate. Read-only. Not yet tested on real hardware.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: OC200 / OC300 hardware controllers (not yet tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Written from the public API and tested against a simulated controller only: please test it on real hardware and report back (see the README).
Errors now name the step that failed. The client list is requested the way more controller versions accept it (fixes 'general error -1' reported by a tester).
Adds a diagnostic report: the plugin's page has a Run diagnostic button (Netlens 0.2.67 or newer) that produces an anonymised description of what the controller answers, to copy or download.

tested_on: TP-Link Omada controller (tested on real hardware by a colleague of the maintainer; model and version to be added)
review.notes: Connection, devices and clients confirmed working on real hardware by a tester; level set by the maintainer. Read-only: one login, a few reads and a logout.

plugins.name: OpenWrt
plugins.description: Reads an OpenWrt router or access point: the router itself as a network node, and every device it knows as a client: DHCP leases and neighbours (wired), and the Wi-Fi stations that are associated with each radio, with band, signal strength (RSSI) and link speed. Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy and to show Wi-Fi signal history and roaming. Read-only: it only calls a few read functions through the router's ubus web interface.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: OPNsense
plugins.description: Reads an OPNsense firewall (24.7 or newer): the firewall itself as the gateway node, and every device in its ARP table as a client, with the manufacturer and host name OPNsense knows, enriched with names from the DHCP leases (Dnsmasq or Kea). Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy under the firewall. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with an API key that may only read these lists.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Pi-hole
plugins.description: Registers your devices in Pi-hole's Local DNS (Pi-hole v6): an A record for every device Netlens knows and DNS does not, and a changed address for devices whose IP changed (DHCP). Pi-hole makes the reverse (PTR) answer by itself. Netlens only changes records it wrote itself (it remembers them, Pi-hole has no comment field) and never touches records you or anything else made.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Pi-hole v5 and older (not supported: different API)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Portainer
plugins.description: Shows every Docker environment that a Portainer manages (local socket, Portainer agents and Edge agents) with its containers: state, health, restarts, image, compose project and published ports. One connection covers all your Docker hosts, without opening each host's Docker port. Read-only: it only lists environments, containers and networks. Kubernetes and Azure environments are skipped.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Portainer CE 2.45 with a local Docker environment (tested)
Portainer agent and Edge environments (not tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: PowerDNS Authoritative
plugins.description: Registers your devices in PowerDNS Authoritative Server (4.x): an A record and a reverse (PTR) record for every device Netlens knows and DNS does not, and a changed address for devices whose IP changed (DHCP). Netlens marks every record set it writes with a comment and only changes or removes record sets that carry it, so records made by anything else are never touched.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Proxmox VE
plugins.description: Built into Netlens: shows which VMs and containers run on which Proxmox host (read-only, API token or password).
plugins.author: Netlens

plugins.name: SNMP switches
plugins.description: Asks managed switches over SNMP v1 / v2c (read-only) which device is plugged into which port: the MAC address table and LLDP. Netlens shows each device's switch and port and places the switches in the hierarchy. Works with switches that have the standard bridge MIB (TP-Link, Netgear, HP / Aruba, Cisco, Zyxel, MikroTik, Ubiquiti and others). Verified against a real device; more switch models are welcome.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Managed switches with SNMP v1/v2c and the BRIDGE-MIB or Q-BRIDGE-MIB (verified on a real device)

releases.changelog: Switches are entered as a list: one line per switch with an optional community of its own (the default community covers the others), a Test button per line, and Test all. Existing settings carry over. Needs Netlens 0.3.109 or newer.
First release. Written from the standard MIBs and tested against simulated switches only: please test it on a real switch and report back (see the README).

plugins.name: Docker Swarm
plugins.description: Shows a Docker Swarm cluster: every node as a host (role, availability, state, address) and every task (a running copy of a service) as a guest of the node it runs on, with service name, stack, image, published ports and state. Read-only through a socket proxy on one manager node. Use the Docker plugin as well if you also want the plain containers and their health.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Synology
plugins.description: Shows a Synology NAS (DiskStation Manager 7) as a host with its Container Manager containers, Virtual Machine Manager machines and installed packages as guests, matched to your network devices by IP or MAC. Read-only, over the DSM web API with HTTPS; needs a dedicated administrator account (DSM has no read-only API role). Tested against a simulated DSM only; a real DS923+ test is pending.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Synology DSM 7.2 (not tested on hardware yet)

releases.changelog: First release. Containers, virtual machines and packages of a Synology NAS as guests of the NAS. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: Technitium DNS
plugins.description: Registers your devices in Technitium DNS Server (A and reverse records) and follows address changes, after a preview and your approval. Works with a primary and secondary server and with a Technitium cluster. It only changes records it created itself and never touches records made by anything else, such as Windows machines that register themselves. Tested on real Technitium 15.5.1 servers (primary and secondary).
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: Technitium DNS Server 15.5.1 with primary and secondary zones (tested on real servers)
Technitium DNS cluster (not yet tested on a real server)

releases.changelog: Servers are entered as a list: one line per server with its own address and token, a Test button per line, and Test all. Existing settings carry over. Needs Netlens 0.3.109 or newer.

tested_on: Technitium DNS Server 15.5.1, primary and secondary pair (real servers)
review.notes: Only the way servers are entered changed (a list with a token per server instead of two comma-separated lists). Checked on the real servers: both lines migrated from the older settings, each tested with its own token, and a sync read both. The write path is unchanged from 1.1.0, which was verified with real writes in a scratch zone.

releases.changelog: Handles CNAME records, so Netlens can give containers that share their host's address a name (add, replace and remove, checked on a real server). Needs Netlens 0.2.106 or newer.

tested_on: Technitium DNS Server 15.5.1, primary and secondary pair (real servers, scratch zone)
review.notes: Adds CNAME add / replace / delete, tested on the real servers in a scratch zone (the record keeps the Netlens comment). Still only touches records carrying the Netlens marker or tracked by Netlens.

releases.changelog: Tested on real Technitium 15.5.1 servers. A PTR delete that finds nothing left (Technitium removes the PTR together with its A record) now counts as done.

tested_on: Technitium DNS Server 15.5.1, primary and secondary pair (real servers, scratch zone)
review.notes: Read: zones and records with comments. Write: one A and one PTR record added, then removed. Only touches records carrying the Netlens marker or tracked by Netlens.

releases.changelog: First release. Written from the official API documentation and tested against a simulated Technitium server only: please try it on a scratch zone first and report back (see the README).

plugins.name: Traefik
plugins.description: Shows the sites a Traefik v2/v3 reverse proxy publishes: domains from the router rules, the upstream address and port, whether TLS is on, and redirects. Netlens ties every site to the device or container behind it, keeps an HTTPS check per site and can give the domains a DNS name. Read-only: it only calls Traefik's API. Traefik does not list the certificates it holds, so certificate expiry is read by Netlens' own HTTPS checks.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: TrueNAS
plugins.description: Shows a TrueNAS (Community Edition 25.04 or newer) as a host with its containers, virtual machines and apps as guests, matched to your network devices by IP or MAC. Read-only, with an API key over TLS. Tested on TrueNAS 25.10.6 (VMs with simulated data).
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: Adds a dashboard card with running and stopped apps, containers and virtual machines. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.
Several TrueNAS systems can be read: one line per system with its own address and API key, a Test button per line, and Test all. Existing settings carry over. Needs Netlens 0.3.109 or newer.

review.notes: Read-only: only reads through the API with a read-only key (https only). Version 25.04 is not tested.

releases.changelog: Guests now carry details: CPU and memory of VMs and containers, and for apps the version, whether an update is available, the image and the ports they publish (the host's Open ports table names the app). Needs Netlens 0.2.106 or newer.
First release. Containers, VMs and apps of a TrueNAS as guests of the NAS.
Adds a diagnostic report: a Run diagnostic button on the plugin's page (Netlens 0.2.67 or newer) shows an anonymised description of what TrueNAS answers, to copy or download.

plugins.name: Ubiquiti UniFi
plugins.description: Reads the UniFi Network application (UniFi OS consoles such as Dream Machine and Cloud Key Gen2+, or a classic self-hosted controller): gateway, switches and access points, which device hangs below which, and which switch or access point each client is connected to, with Wi-Fi signal, band and link rate. Read-only. Not yet tested on real hardware.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: UniFi OS consoles (Dream Machine, Cloud Gateway, Cloud Key Gen2+) (not yet tested)
Classic self-hosted controller, port 8443 (not yet tested)

releases.changelog: First release. Written from the public API and tested against a simulated controller only: please test it on real hardware and report back (see the README).
Adds a diagnostic report: a Run diagnostic button on the plugin's page (Netlens 0.2.67 or newer) shows an anonymised description of what the controller answers, to copy or download.

plugins.name: VMware ESXi / vCenter
plugins.description: Shows VMware ESXi hosts and vCenter inventories: every host (connection state, management address) and every virtual machine as a guest of its host, with power state, MAC and IP addresses (from VMware Tools), guest operating system, CPUs and memory. Works with a standalone ESXi and with vCenter through VMware's SOAP web service, read-only: it only reads properties. Use an account with the Read-only role.
plugins.author: Netlens
supports: VMware ESXi and vCenter (not tested on real systems)

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.

plugins.name: VyOS
plugins.description: Reads a VyOS router (1.4 or newer): the router itself as a network node (host name, version, interface MAC addresses) and every device in its ARP table and DHCP server leases as a client, with the interface it is reached on. Netlens uses this to place devices in the hierarchy under the router. Read-only: it only sends show and showConfig requests to VyOS's HTTPS API.
plugins.author: Netlens

releases.changelog: First release. Needs Netlens 0.3.157 or newer.
